environment: Windows, .NET 10, AMD Ryzen 9 3950X (16 physical / 32 logical cores)
reuse: System.Buffers.ArrayPool<double> supplies private scratch; published series are never pooled
result: Shared kernels now accelerate independent Full-history SMA and Asin. Worker-local scratch improves SMA over the rejected direct-ring prototype. LatestOnly SMA remains behind the strongest parallel native result in the final paired sweep.
limitations: Steady-state short runs; earlier builder-only SMA means were lower and do not establish a strongest-native win.

At 100k/period20 the scratch pool needs roughly 1 MiB of capacity per active SMA dispatch. It can retain buffers across sizes/threads; allocation-per-operation excludes warmed retained scratch and cold pool growth.
Full history retains an owned bar array; LatestOnly and native values-only payloads are smaller.
Native arms omit validation, snapshots, and Asin presence. Native parallel decimal SMA permits 1e-10 tolerance; builder output is checked against its existing bitwise contract.
Asin presence remains a fully materialized double column. No deferred-output allocation is counted as a win.
GPU regression checks passed; this batch adds no GPU crossover claim or general indicator rollout.
Worker policy is measured on this CPU, not universal hardware qualification. Pool initialization and external dispatch contention are excluded.
Ring-candidate SMA rows are rejected evidence. Its Asin implementation is retained; final SMA conclusions use policy-paired-final rows.
